_doc: What each agent may CHANGE, verified after the fact by `arcanium-runs changed --agent <name>`.
`tools:` in a subagent definition is a capability list, not a sandbox. Two holes:
* bash runs anything - an agent given bash to run tests can also run `git checkout`.
* write reaches any path, not only the one it was granted the tool for.
So permission is verified against the repo itself, not trusted at the prompt.
[]        = read-only; ANY change is a breach
[...]     = only these; a trailing / covers a subtree, otherwise glob

_notes.reviewer: Has `tools: read, bash`. bash is the hole - it can write via `sh -c 'cat > f'` or destroy work via `git checkout`. quality/adversarial-review says the reviewer changes nothing; [] is that rule made checkable.
_notes.fixer: quality/mechanical-fix limits it to narrow patches. It may not touch pyproject.toml or docs - a dependency change is re-scoping, which is the implementer's call.
_notes.implementer: Frozen gates are NOT covered here. `arcanium-runs freeze` guards those by content hash, which is stricter: it holds even for paths inside this allowlist.
